items.stem: Algorithm: if n is even, replace n by n/2; if n is odd, replace n by 3n + 1; stop when n = 1. Starting with n = 7, how many replacements are made before stopping?
items.markingKey: Trace the sequence from 7 to 1: 16 steps.

items.stem: A librarian wants to arrange 6 books by their accession numbers 58, 24, 28, 45, 13, 36. (i) Write the list after the first pass of bubble sort. (ii) How many passes are needed until a pass makes no swaps? (iii) In the sorted list, how many comparisons does binary search need to find 28? (iv) Why sort first?
items.answer: (i) 24, 28, 45, 13, 36, 58 (ii) 5 (iii) at most 3 (iv) binary search needs a sorted list
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part; (i) largest number moves to the end.

items.stem: A shop billing flowchart: Start → read price P → if P ≥ ₹1500, give 20% discount, else no discount → add 5% GST on the amount after discount → output bill → End. (i) Name the shape used for "if P ≥ ₹1500". (ii) Find the bill for P = ₹500. (iii) Find the bill for P = ₹2000. (iv) Write the steps as a numbered algorithm.
items.answer: (i) diamond (ii) ₹525 (iii) ₹1,680 (iv) 1. Read P 2. If P ≥ 1500, P = P − 20% of P 3. Bill = 1.05P 4. Output bill
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem: A school has 224 notebooks and 108 pencils to pack into identical kits, with no item left over and each kit having the same number of notebooks and the same number of pencils. (i) Use Euclid's algorithm to find the greatest number of kits. (ii) How many notebooks and pencils are in each kit? (iii) How many division steps did the algorithm take?
items.answer: (i) 4 kits (ii) 56 notebooks and 27 pencils (iii) 3
